ranked_candidates.title: Rogers–Szegő local ordinary discriminants and arithmetic
ranked_candidates.plain_meaning: Describes exactly how repeated Rogers–Szegő roots split when q moves away from a fixed root of unity, including the extra collision at −1, and computes the first nonzero ordinary discriminant coefficient.
ranked_candidates.exact_claim:
Let H_n(z;q)=sum_k [n choose k]_q z^k, D_n(q)=Disc_z H_n, n=Ad+b, d odd, ω primitive of order d, and q(ε)=ω(1+ε²)^(1/d). Put F=z^d+1 and P_A=product_(j=1)^A j^j.
Separated case: G=H_b(z;ω), 0≤b<d, A≥1, Disc(G)Res(F,G)≠0. At α^d=−1, H_n(α+εx;q(ε))=ε^A(−1)^A d^(A/2)G(α)He_A(√d x/α)+O(ε^(A+1)). With K=dA(A−1)/2, D_n(q(ε))=ε^(2K)(C+O(ε²)), C=(−1)^(A(d−1)/2)d^(dA(A+1)/2)P_A^d Disc(G)Res(F,G)^(2A). Thus ord_(Φ_d)D_n=K.
Simple-overlap case: d≥3, b odd with 1≤b<d. Write G=(z+1)U, g=U(−1), W=(ω;ω)_b/(ω²;ω²)_((b+d)/2), τ=dW/g and J_(A+1)=He_(A+1)+A(1−τ)He_(A−1). If g≠0, H_n(−1+εx;q(ε))=ε^(A+1)(−1)^(A+1)d^((A−1)/2)g J_(A+1)(−√d x;τ)+O(ε^(A+2)).
If additionally Disc(U)Res(F,U)Disc(J_(A+1))≠0, L=dA(A−1)/2+A and D_n(q(ε))=ε^(2L)(C+O(ε²)), C=(−1)^(A(d−1)/2)d^(dA(A+1)/2+A)P_A^(d−1)Disc(J_(A+1))Disc(U)Res(F,U)^(2A)g². Hence ord_(Φ_d)D_n=L. Square roots cancel coefficientwise.
ranked_candidates.model: Characteristic-zero formal series; ordinary z-derivative discriminant; arbitrary fixed odd d with the stated residual guards. Disc(1)=1.
ranked_candidates.proof_status: Both separated and overlap theorems were accepted in saved independent audits. This catalogue re-read the proofs and qualifications, but did not repeat their computations or create a fresh independent correctness audit.
ranked_candidates.inspection_status: Theorem/audit source read as inert text; no supplied program execution
ranked_candidates.novelty_status: Plausible specific theorem package; external priority remains unresolved. Standard q-Lucas, Hermite limits, quasi-Laguerre discriminants and hook-Wronskian theory are not new.
ranked_candidates.novelty_delta: The narrow candidate is the explicitly normalized fixed-nontrivial-ω, moving-z local coefficient, especially τ and the shared-root coefficient, together with its full ordinary discriminant and arithmetic use.
ranked_candidates.significance: Ranks first in this domain: uniform exact formulas with independent proof audits, coherent special-functions/arithmetic consequences, and a more visible substantive increment than isolated certificate or standard-ingredient applications.
ranked_candidates.publication_readiness: Best algebra manuscript-development core; needs self-contained exposition and legitimate full-text priority comparisons, especially Lubinsky–Saff 1987 and Zhedanov 1997. No originality announcement warranted.
ranked_candidates.limitations: Only separated or exactly one simple shared residual root at −1. Nonzero residual discriminant/resultant and Disc J are essential. No arbitrary-overlap, repeated-p, all-composite, or globally cleared novelty theorem.
ranked_candidates.rank_rationale: The strongest coherent specialized mathematical package: growing-degree local coefficients, exact ordinary-discriminant leading terms and arithmetic consequences. Its fixed-root local increment is precise; two close older full-text comparisons remain open.
ranked_candidates.next_check: Full legitimate comparison with Lubinsky–Saff (1987), Zhedanov (1997), and citing local-root/discriminant literature; retain all residual guards.

ranked_candidates.title: Sharp dyadic Fourier endpoint minimax N/4+1
ranked_candidates.plain_meaning: Even the best independent row and column ordering leaves a precisely determined large cut rank.
ranked_candidates.exact_claim: For N=2^m≥8 in characteristic zero, min_(ρ,σ) q(Pρ F_N Pσ^T)=N/4+1, attained by double bit reversal. r_N(k)=ceil(k/2)+r_(N/4)(floor(k/2)) for k≤N/2 with reflection; total upper-cut sum is exactly minimal at N8,16 (14,48), and bit reversal has leading asymptotic N²/6.
ranked_candidates.model: Single-matrix exact quasiseparable rank; all independent endpoint permutations, characteristic zero.
ranked_candidates.inspection_status: Internally independently audited within stated scope; not external peer review or priority certification

ranked_candidates.novelty_delta: Candidate delta is universal second-moment/odd-cardinality lower bound matching a known digit-reversal hierarchy. TW470 already gives digit-reversal rank-one grids/support uncertainty. Final2008 comparison unresolved.
ranked_candidates.significance: Cleanest sharp all-size structural theorem in this census; broad intrinsic invariant and short proof. Priority risk from final Delvaux comparison prevents a first/best-known claim.
ranked_candidates.publication_readiness: Not externally peer reviewed; priority and manuscript-readiness remain separate from mathematical support

ranked_candidates.rank_rationale: A sharp all-dyadic-size extremal theorem under arbitrary independent endpoint permutations. The universal second-moment lower bound is the potential increment; the attaining bit-reversal hierarchy is classical.

Fixed dyadic 0<epsilon<=1/4 or epsilon=2^-ceil((log2N)^beta), fixed0<beta<1: O_epsilon(Nlog N/loglog N) word ops,O(N) words. Efficiently supplied precision p=o(log N) yields o(Nlog N).
ranked_candidates.model: Address-capable word RAM w=Theta(log N), integer arithmetic/shifts/division; coefficients use O(log N+p) bits. Finite binary input and efficiently available precision parameter.
ranked_candidates.cost_and_charges: All cold padded tables, root/phase approximants, normalization, exact scaling, input/output, packing, guards and addresses paid. Alphabet b=O(p+loglog N), largest dyadic m with mb<=gamma log2N; setup N^gamma polylog N for fixed gamma<1.

ranked_candidates.proof_status: New full paper proof survives two independent read-only reviews at fixed epsilon; no supplied code execution. General merely computable precision schedule must be qualified by its computation cost.

ranked_candidates.title: Exact Green length three for an arithmetic five-dimensional family
ranked_candidates.plain_meaning: A specific infinite parameter family of five-by-five matrices needs exactly three allowed Green terms.
ranked_candidates.exact_claim: For N=5q² with q positive odd, gcd(q,5)=1 and q≡1 mod241, the block C_q=B_N[S,S], S={0,q²,2q²,3q²,4q²}, B_N=(F_N^−1+diag(ω^((N+1)j²/2)))^−1, has exact minimum three diagonally ended Hamiltonian cyclic resolvents over a genuine quadratic extension of Q(η), η=ω^(q⁴). Upper representation has two nontrivial reciprocal-holonomy branches and one diagonal zero-weight branch.
ranked_candidates.model: Fixed dimension5, infinitely many arithmetic parameters. All cycle orders, legal denominators, zero edge weights and singular endpoint masks included in lower bound.
ranked_candidates.inspection_status: Internally independently audited within stated scope; not external peer review or priority certification
ranked_candidates.novelty_status: Unresolved worldwide priority; negative search results are not novelty proof.
ranked_candidates.novelty_delta: Matched exact additive length is not supplied by generic multiplicative diagonal–circulant factorization or inverse-band representation theory. Lower certificate is geometric-fiber emptiness across576 ordered pairs, not a finite rational-point scan; upper guards are uniform local-ring arguments.
ranked_candidates.significance: Most concrete certificate-intensive additive-length novelty candidate, but specialized fixed dimension reduces breadth versus C02.
ranked_candidates.publication_readiness: Not externally peer reviewed; priority and manuscript-readiness remain separate from mathematical support
ranked_candidates.limitations: Not a growing-dimensional upper family. Base-field-only upper length is unproved. Full B_N inherits only ≥3. No full uniformly cheap B_N or Fourier speedup.
ranked_candidates.rank_rationale: Exceptionally concrete matching upper/lower theorem with all-order, boundary-inclusive certification. Below the first three because the upper construction remains fixed at 5×5, even though parameters and ambient dimensions grow.
ranked_candidates.next_check: Focused additive cyclic-resolvent/secant-sum literature comparison; concise certificate-and-proof exposition with field of definition explicit.

ranked_candidates.title: Bounded-separator independently routed inverse sums
ranked_candidates.plain_meaning: A flat Fourier-like unitary cannot be a constant-sized sum of independently routed inverses with small graph separators.
ranked_candidates.exact_claim: For complex flat unitary U, r≥1 and T=Σ_i L_i Q_i^−1 R_i with permutation-contained endpoint supports, if every required marked restriction of each symmetric bipartite support lift has a half-balanced separator≤q, U=T implies N≤4qr36^r; U=D+T implies N≤16qr36^r. Treewidth w gives q=w+1. Invertible column-two Q gives q=3, hence12r36^r/48r36^r. Fixed r,q prevent vanishing operator or normalized Frobenius error.
ranked_candidates.model: Exact independently routed sums, arbitrary zero endpoint weights; no row-degree restriction. Complex norm/flat-unitary comparison.
ranked_candidates.inspection_status: Internally independently audited within stated scope; not external peer review or priority certification
ranked_candidates.novelty_status: Unresolved worldwide priority; negative search results are not novelty proof.
ranked_candidates.novelty_delta: Actual extension beyond inherited separation theorem is attached trees/high-degree column-two supports and general bounded vertex separators. Inverse-nullity, weighted centroid separators, GIRS and bare-cycle logarithmic bounds are antecedents. Tree witness verifies new structural coverage.
ranked_candidates.significance: Broader target/support theorem and coherent short-note candidate using classical tools; strongest new separator-family statement, behind sharp C02 and matched C01 in this structural ranking.
ranked_candidates.publication_readiness: Not externally peer reviewed; priority and manuscript-readiness remain separate from mathematical support
ranked_candidates.limitations: Term count≠runtime. No products/shared evaluator bound; fixed positive-error tolerance does not automatically force logarithmic r. Independent routing and bare-cycle multiplicity were already covered.
ranked_candidates.rank_rationale: A broad, clean restricted-representation obstruction with a now-proved structural non-containment witness. Classical inverse-nullity/separator tools and inherited independent-routing machinery narrow the novelty increment.

ranked_candidates.exact_claim: Odd N: Fourier Weyl coefficient matrix has rank N. Canonical ordered G_S(α)G_T(β) with Weyl-monomial endpoints has coefficient rank≤1, so B≥N. Rotated pair U=S^uT^v,V=S^rT^s has Fourier coefficient rank N/gcd(N,δ), δ=(us−vr−ur−vs)/2. For odd prime p, any single fixed generating pair shared by all branches, without extra Weyl endpoints, needs B≥(p+1)/2.
ranked_candidates.model: Ordered depth-two paths in one fixed Weyl basis/pair. Canonical endpoint allowance is different from fixed-pair Hankel theorem.
ranked_candidates.inspection_status: Internally independently audited within stated scope; not external peer review or priority certification
ranked_candidates.novelty_status: Unresolved worldwide priority; negative search results are not novelty proof.
ranked_candidates.novelty_delta: Candidate restricted grammar combination of classical Weyl/Gauss and Hankel/Vandermonde arguments. Not C05, C04 or separator A.
ranked_candidates.significance: Strong numerical branch count but narrow grammar and elementary rank mechanism; useful focused theorem or section, global priority unresolved.
ranked_candidates.publication_readiness: Not externally peer reviewed; priority and manuscript-readiness remain separate from mathematical support
ranked_candidates.limitations: Changing generators can collapse coefficient rank to1. Reverse order and depth3 give full coefficient rank with O(N) application; mixed orders/generators/arbitrary diagonal gauges outside bounds.
ranked_candidates.rank_rationale: Strong exact branch counts and useful basis-sensitive counterexamples, but narrow grammars and classical coefficient/Hankel rank mechanisms limit broader significance.
ranked_candidates.next_check: Representation-theoretic and Prony/separation-rank comparison for the exact ordered grammar; never infer general runtime from coefficient rank.

ranked_candidates.title: Exact scalar common-cycle chirp-resolvent bank minima
ranked_candidates.plain_meaning: Determines the fewest first-order resolvents of one fixed cycle needed to synthesize an odd quadratic chirp, and how one free diagonal changes that answer.
ranked_candidates.exact_claim:
For N=2m+1≥3, primitive q in characteristic zero, h=(N+1)/2, f(k)=q^(hk²), C=sum_(k=0)^(N−1)f(k)P^k, represent C=sum_(s=1)^Q a_s(I−λ_sP)^(−1), with a_s,λ_s≠0 and λ_s^N≠1. Without a free diagonal Qmin=m+1 for every odd N.
With δI free, Qmin=m iff T_m(z)=(-1)^mH_m(−z;q) has simple nonzero nonresonant roots; otherwise Qmin=m+1. An arbitrary free diagonal does not enlarge this scalar common-P circulant model.
T_m(0)=(-1)^m. gcd(T_m,z^N−1)=1 for N≡1 mod4 and z−1 for N≡3 mod4, the latter root simple. Thus all N≡3 mod4 have Qmin=m+1. Every prime N≡1 mod4 and the audited infinite families have Qmin=m.
When Qmin=m, δ=(-1)^m q^(−m(m+1)/2)product_(j=1)^m(1−q^j) is forced and nonzero. Nodes/weights may lie in an algebraic closure; root-free sum works over Q(q).
ranked_candidates.model: Scalar coefficients, same natural cycle P, first-order nonconfluent resolvents, no branch-dependent diagonal endpoints or independent routing.
ranked_candidates.proof_status: Uniform construction/minimum and partial free-diagonal classification independently accepted. Nonsingular Hankel lower bound and guarded polynomial-pencil upper construction both checked.

ranked_candidates.novelty_delta: Exact legal-node count in this fixed grammar, uniform resonance classification, forced diagonal and explicit root-free construction. This is distinct from the five-coordinate all-order Green exact-three theorem.
ranked_candidates.significance: Ranks fourth: a genuine exact minimum with strong proofs, but its grammar is narrow and core moment mechanisms old; the unresolved general composite guard precludes a full closed-form classification.
ranked_candidates.publication_readiness: Substantive restricted-model theorem, best application/companion section to RS work or Green realization note; broad standalone significance less clear.

all_rows.title: Local ordinary discriminants at odd roots of unity
all_rows.plain_meaning: Describes exactly how repeated Rogers–Szegő roots split when q moves away from a fixed root of unity, including the extra collision at −1, and computes the first nonzero ordinary discriminant coefficient.
all_rows.exact_claim:
Let H_n(z;q)=sum_k [n choose k]_q z^k, D_n(q)=Disc_z H_n, n=Ad+b, d odd, ω primitive of order d, and q(ε)=ω(1+ε²)^(1/d). Put F=z^d+1 and P_A=product_(j=1)^A j^j.
Separated case: G=H_b(z;ω), 0≤b<d, A≥1, Disc(G)Res(F,G)≠0. At α^d=−1, H_n(α+εx;q(ε))=ε^A(−1)^A d^(A/2)G(α)He_A(√d x/α)+O(ε^(A+1)). With K=dA(A−1)/2, D_n(q(ε))=ε^(2K)(C+O(ε²)), C=(−1)^(A(d−1)/2)d^(dA(A+1)/2)P_A^d Disc(G)Res(F,G)^(2A). Thus ord_(Φ_d)D_n=K.
Simple-overlap case: d≥3, b odd with 1≤b<d. Write G=(z+1)U, g=U(−1), W=(ω;ω)_b/(ω²;ω²)_((b+d)/2), τ=dW/g and J_(A+1)=He_(A+1)+A(1−τ)He_(A−1). If g≠0, H_n(−1+εx;q(ε))=ε^(A+1)(−1)^(A+1)d^((A−1)/2)g J_(A+1)(−√d x;τ)+O(ε^(A+2)).
If additionally Disc(U)Res(F,U)Disc(J_(A+1))≠0, L=dA(A−1)/2+A and D_n(q(ε))=ε^(2L)(C+O(ε²)), C=(−1)^(A(d−1)/2)d^(dA(A+1)/2+A)P_A^(d−1)Disc(J_(A+1))Disc(U)Res(F,U)^(2A)g². Hence ord_(Φ_d)D_n=L. Square roots cancel coefficientwise.
all_rows.model: Characteristic-zero formal series; ordinary z-derivative discriminant; arbitrary fixed odd d with the stated residual guards. Disc(1)=1.
all_rows.proof_status: Both separated and overlap theorems were accepted in saved independent audits. This catalogue re-read the proofs and qualifications, but did not repeat their computations or create a fresh independent correctness audit.

all_rows.novelty_delta: The narrow candidate is the explicitly normalized fixed-nontrivial-ω, moving-z local coefficient, especially τ and the shared-root coefficient, together with its full ordinary discriminant and arithmetic use.

all_rows.title: Nonzero one-window common-chirp phase eliminant
all_rows.plain_meaning: Turns an unknown common quadratic phase into a bounded list of algebraic candidates from one short data window.
all_rows.exact_claim:
For r≥1, N≥3r, F_p containing supplied ω of exact order N, a nonzero x_j=ω^(aj²)sum_(ℓ=1)^s c_ℓω^(b_ℓj), s≤r, has a nonzero center c in [r,N−r−1]. Put h=c−r.
P_h(t)=t^(−E)det[x_(h+i+j)t^binom(i+j,2)]_(i,j=0)^r is a polynomial, E=(r+1)r(r−1)/2. It has degree at most D=binom(r+2,3), constant coefficient (−1)^(r(r+1)/2)x_c^(r+1)≠0, and P_h(ω^(−2a))=0 for every valid phase.
There are at most min(D,N/gcd(2,N)) canonical phase candidates. For even N phases a and a+N/2 are equivalent after frequency translation. The all-zero input is rank-zero and must be handled separately.
all_rows.model: Exact finite-field root-of-unity grid, bounded common chirp rank; N≥3r is a witness guarantee, not a universal identifiability threshold.
all_rows.proof_status: Accepted independent audit of the full recognition theorem; polynomial proof uses unique extremal determinant terms, not fitted degrees. Catalogue has inspected theorem/audit text; no source program executed.
all_rows.inspection_status: Theorem/audit source read as inert text; no supplied program execution

all_rows.significance: Ranks above the reciprocal-pencil formula because the nonzero witness gives a concrete all-input recognition mechanism and avoids degeneracy-based completeness gaps, while retaining limited fixed-r structured-input scope.
all_rows.publication_readiness: Good secondary algorithm/algebra note candidate after broader algebraic chirp-identification comparison; strongest in combination with charged exact recognition.
